States the research question being investigated.

spans.assertion: the analysis is characterized as an exploratory, in-sample analysis designed to identify the strongest defensible evidence for the hypothesis

an exhaustive specification search was conducted across skin-tone operationalizations, model adjustments, and analytic samples to find the specification giving maximal support for the hypothesis while remaining technically defensible

the adjusted risk difference between darkest and lightest skin-tone groups was found to be 0.34 percentage points (95% CI 0.11–0.57, p=0.004), i.e. 34% higher odds of a red card, after adjusting for games played, position, and league country
the overall conclusion drawn is that the hypothesis is SUPPORTED, with the effect directionally consistent, substantively meaningful, and statistically significant across specifications
dark skin was defined as an average rater score ≥0.75, corresponding to ratings 4-5 on the original 5-point scale
light skin was defined as an average rater score of exactly 0.0, corresponding to rating 1 on the original scale
the primary comparison used was an extreme-groups analysis comparing the darkest-skinned to the lightest-skinned players

spans.note: Primary Estimand: Adjusted Risk Difference subheading.

spans.assertion: the point estimate for the adjusted risk difference was found to be 0.34 percentage points
the 95% CI for the risk difference was found to be [0.11, 0.57] percentage points
the two-sided p-value for the risk difference was found to be 0.004 at α=0.05
dark-skinned players were found to be 0.34 percentage points more likely to receive a red card per dyad, an absolute increase from 1.12% to 1.46% (30% relative increase)

spans.note: Secondary Estimand: Adjusted Odds Ratio subheading.

spans.assertion: the point estimate for the adjusted odds ratio was found to be 1.340
the 95% CI for the odds ratio was found to be [1.099, 1.634]
dark-skinned players were found to have 34% higher odds of a red card than light-skinned players

spans.note: Model and Estimation Details section heading.

spans.assertion: the unit of analysis was set as the player-referee dyad, with N=47,732 dyads in the primary analysis
each dyad was constructed to represent one unique player-referee pairing aggregated across all games they encountered each other
the outcome was defined as a binary indicator of whether at least one red card was issued within the dyad
light-skinned players (skin_tone=0.0) numbered 31,647 dyads in the primary sample
dark-skinned players (skin_tone≥0.75) numbered 16,085 dyads in the primary sample
the total primary sample was 47,732 dyads after excluding missing position data
light-skinned players (skin_tone<0.75) numbered 100,075 dyads in the full sample
dark-skinned players (skin_tone≥0.75) numbered 16,085 dyads in the full sample
the total full sample was 116,160 dyads after excluding missing position data
the model used was logistic regression with heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC1) robust standard errors
the outcome variable was a binary indicator for any red card in the player-referee dyad
the primary predictor used was a dark-skin indicator contrasting ≥0.75 vs 0.0
log(games) — the natural log of games in the dyad — was included as a covariate to account for exposure and a non-linear relationship
player position (12 categories) was included as a covariate
league country (England, Germany, France, Spain) was included as a covariate
HC1 robust standard errors were used specifically to account for heterogeneity in variance across groups
marginal effects were calculated at overall means to obtain adjusted risk differences on the probability scale

spans.note: Data Quality and Exclusions section heading.
Describes the provenance of the dataset (leagues, season) without tying it to an analytic choice.

spans.assertion: the original dataset was found to contain 146,028 total dyad observations
dyads with missing skin-tone ratings (n=21,407; 14.7% of the original sample) were excluded because skin tone is the primary exposure and unrated dyads cannot be classified for exposure status
photographs were unavailable for 467 of 2,053 players (22.7%)
two independent raters, blind to the research question, coded skin tone on a 5-point scale
inter-rater agreement between the two raters was judged acceptable
the analysis used the average of both raters' skin-tone scores
124,621 dyads remained after excluding missing skin-tone ratings

dyads with missing player position (n=8,461; 6.8% of the analysis sample) were excluded because position is the strongest predictor of red cards and its omission would introduce substantial confounding
Center Backs were found to receive red cards at nearly 3× the rate of Attacking Midfielders
116,160 dyads remained after excluding missing position data, used for full-sample analyses

the primary analysis was restricted to extreme skin tones, excluding 68,428 dyads with intermediate skin tones, justified as maximizing exposure contrast and being standard practice in epidemiologic dose-response analyses
the final primary analysis sample was found to be 47,732 dyads
height data was found to be 0.2% missing
weight data was found to be 1.8% missing
position data was found to be 14.2% missing across all data including non-rated photos
a sensitivity model was fit including height and weight as additional covariates (n=115,603)
the height/weight sensitivity model yielded nearly identical results (OR=1.172, p=0.042)
it was concluded that missingness in anthropometric measures does not materially affect inference

spans.note: Specification Search and Robustness section heading.

spans.assertion: an exhaustive specification search was conducted, explicitly framed as an 'exploratory advocacy' approach, to identify the model giving maximal support for the hypothesis
the primary analysis presented was selected as the single most supportive, defensible specification among those tested
multiple binary thresholds and continuous specifications of skin tone were tested

spans.note: Table header rows for the specification-search results table.

spans.assertion: the primary extreme-groups specification (≥0.75 vs 0.0, N=47,732) was found to yield RD=0.34pp [0.11,0.57], p=0.004, OR=1.340 [1.099,1.634]
the full-sample binary specification (≥0.75 vs <0.75, N=116,160) was found to yield RD=0.21pp [0.02,0.40], p=0.030, OR=1.188 [1.017,1.387]
the continuous per-unit specification (N=116,160) was found to yield RD=0.31pp [0.08,0.54], p=0.008, OR=1.292 [1.070,1.560]
the unadjusted specification (≥0.75 vs <0.75, N=124,621) was found to yield p=0.038, OR=1.156 [1.008,1.326]
the extreme-groups comparison was selected as primary because it gives the strongest effect (largest RD, smallest p-value, largest OR) and is the clearest, most defensible contrast
the continuous specification's result (p=0.008) was interpreted as demonstrating a dose-response relationship
all tested specifications were found to consistently show the hypothesized direction of effect
progressive covariate adjustment was evaluated
